title: Milestone Achievement Roadmap Strategy (MARS)
opening: A nearer result helps when it moves you toward the larger goal or tells you what needs to change. MARS connects that result with what you try next.

labels.comparison: Will fifty pages help someone learn?
labels.comparisonIntro: Suppose a teacher wants people to use a method independently. Publishing fifty pages is one possible task. Compare finishing those pages with finding out whether someone can actually use the method.
labels.adherenceText: The larger aim is for people to use the method independently. A useful nearer result must improve that ability or tell the teacher what help is missing.
labels.valueText: A person trying the method without the teacher supplying every answer could reveal what they can use. Until that attempt happens, the teacher has a proposed milestone and a question, not an achieved result.
labels.outcomeText: Arrange one suitable attempt and observe where help is needed. If the person succeeds, choose what to extend; if they get stuck, revise the method or support before adding more pages.
labels.signalQuestion: Choose a part of the comparison
labels.rhythmTitle: What the four parts of MARS do
labels.rhythmText: The Milestone is the nearer result that matters to the larger goal. Achievement means noticing when you reach it and what it shows. The Roadmap connects it to the larger direction, and Strategy is how you approach the next result. Missing a milestone can reveal something useful too. A month or quarter may fit the work, but the date alone does not make a result valuable. If one direct action can finish the goal, you do not need a roadmap.
labels.practice: Choose a nearer result that changes what comes next
labels.practiceIntro: Keep the notes that help you decide what to try or change. You can save a partial note and return after the attempt.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six course questions remain separate.

labels.sourceQuote:
Milestone Achievement Roadmap Strategy (MARS)
Choose a distant goal that feels daunting. What nearer result could you work toward
this month or quarter? In MARS, that result is the Milestone; notice the
Achievement when you reach it, place it on the Roadmap toward your larger goal
and choose the Strategy for reaching the next one. Review what reaching or missing
it reveals.

fields.label: The larger goal and why it matters
A nearer result worth working toward

example.qualities: Help people use a teaching method independently.
example.contribution: Have one willing person try the method on a suitable question.
example.avoid: Their attempt can reveal whether the instructions give enough help and where they need work.
example.connection: Arrange the attempt, leave room for their reasoning, then ask what helped and what was unclear.
example.change: If finishing the instructions does not help someone use them, revise them before expanding the course.
